CHAPTER 6

Exploring and Modifying Unfamiliar Systems
探索与改造陌生系统

Some of the most valuable experience I gained was from supporting a legacy app. I highly recommend it, but I wouldn’t wish it on anyone.
——Dalia Abo Sheasha, software developer

我获得的最宝贵经验，有一部分来自维护一个遗留应用。我强烈推荐这种经历，但我也不希望它落在任何人头上。
——Dalia Abo Sheasha，软件开发者

While many developers love the blank canvas of greenfield projects, the harsh reality of software development is that most of the work we do will be on established systems. Don’t let this reality discourage your view on the profession of software development. Working with existing codebases has its advantages. Many key decisions have already been made, allowing you to focus directly on the problems at hand instead of worrying about infrastructure.

虽然许多开发者喜欢全新项目的空白画布，但软件开发的残酷现实是：我们做的大多数工作都是在既有系统上。别让这个现实打击你对软件开发职业的看法。在既有代码库上工作有它的好处：许多关键决策已经做好了，让你可以直接专注于手头的问题，而不必担心基础设施。

As someone getting onboarded to a new project or simply exploring a new codebase, you will need to develop skills to explore and modify unfamiliar systems. In this chapter, you’ll discover how to navigate and understand unfamiliar code and how to make changes safely. Whether you’re joining a new team or maintaining legacy systems, these skills will help you confidently contribute to any codebase. This builds on the mechanics of reading code that we covered in Chapter 2.

作为一个刚加入新项目、或仅仅在探索新代码库的人，你需要培养探索和改造陌生系统的技能。在本章中，你会发现如何导航和理解陌生代码，以及如何安全地做出改动。无论你是加入新团队还是维护遗留系统，这些技能都会帮你自信地为任何代码库做贡献。本章建立在第 2 章讲过的读代码基本功之上。

Understanding Unfamiliar Codebases

Whether you’re onboarding at a new company or moving to a new project at your current employer, working with unfamiliar codebases can be stressful and anxiety inducing. This can be caused by the unknown or working with languages, frameworks, or tools that you aren’t familiar with. However, if you approach this challenge with a clear plan and techniques to navigate these uncharted waters, you’ll boost both your success rate and confidence.

无论你是新入职一家公司，还是在当前公司转到新项目，与陌生代码库打交道都可能令人紧张焦虑。这可能是因为未知，也可能是因为在用你不熟悉的语言、框架或工具。然而，如果你带着清晰的计划和驾驭这片未知水域的技巧来应对这个挑战，你的成功率和信心都会提升。

In this section, you will learn techniques for understanding the big picture or goals of the project. You’ll learn how to get familiar with a new project by following the flow or execution path of the code. Finally, you’ll learn how to incrementally build mental models by breaking complex systems into manageable pieces. As you work through this chapter or explore a new project, remember that it’s OK to not immediately understand everything in a new codebase. Even team members who have worked on the project for years don’t know everything about it.

在本节中，你将学习理解项目全局或目标的技巧。你将学习如何通过跟随代码的流程或执行路径来熟悉一个新项目。最后，你将学习如何把复杂系统拆成可管理的小块，逐步建立心智模型。当你学习本章或探索新项目时，请记住：在新代码库里不能立刻理解一切是完全正常的。即使在项目上干了多年的团队成员，也并非对它了如指掌。

Start with the Big Picture

“You can’t see the forest through the trees.” This means that if you’re so focused on tiny details (which version of your framework you’re using), you fail to understand the bigger picture or overall situation (the goal of this project). You probably want to dive in and start contributing to the project and proving your worth to the team right away. It’s always nice to have a plan, and here are some tips for getting a grasp on the big picture.

“只见树木，不见森林。”意思是：如果你太专注于微小细节（比如你用的是框架的哪个版本），你就无法理解全局或整体形势（这个项目的目标）。你大概想一头扎进去，立刻开始为项目做贡献、向团队证明你的价值。有个计划总是好的，下面是一些把握全局的技巧。

Understanding the project

Before you can begin to even understand the code, you need to understand the purpose and intent of the project. Start with a high level: what is the overall reason for this project existing? Who are the stakeholders of this project? What does this project mean to your employer? Is it a large part of the business?

在你甚至开始理解代码之前，你需要理解项目的目的和意图。从高层开始：这个项目为什么存在？谁是它的利益相关者？这个项目对你的雇主意味着什么？它是业务的重要组成部分吗？

There are many ways to do this, but a good place to start is with someone who has deep knowledge of the product, like a product manager. See if you can set up a meeting with this person and be prepared to learn. Take notes as much as you can so that you can refer back to them later. If this is a virtual meeting, ask if you can record it so you can review it again later. Most importantly, ask questions. The only dumb questions are the ones you don’t ask.

做法有很多，但一个好的起点是找一个对产品有深入了解的人，比如产品经理。看看能不能约这个人开个会，做好学习的准备。尽量多做笔记，以便日后回看。如果是线上会议，问问能不能录屏，方便以后复习。最重要的是：提问。唯一愚蠢的问题是你没问出口的那个。

After talking with a product owner and getting a high-level overview of the project, it’s time to dive deeper into the technical side of things. At this point, reach out to any software engineers who currently work on the project, and if you can find any who originally developed the system, consider this like striking gold during the gold rush. Ideally, you will want to reach out to someone in a tech lead or architecture role who can provide valuable insights about decisions that were made.

和产品负责人聊过、对项目有了高层概览之后，是时候往技术侧深挖了。这时，联系目前在项目上工作的软件工程师；如果你能找到最初开发这套系统的人，就像淘金热里淘到了金子。最理想的是找一个技术负责人或架构师角色的人，他们能对当初的决策提供宝贵洞见。

Who are the customers of this product? Go out and find any public information about this project. If there is any, try to look at this from the customers’ perspective. Some companies develop user personas for their products, which are fictional profiles of the actual users that can help you understand different types of users, their goals, and pain points. This will give you valuable context for why certain technical decisions were made.

这个产品的客户是谁？去找一找关于这个项目的公开信息。如果有，试着从客户的视角看。有些公司会为产品建立用户画像，即真实用户的虚构档案，帮你理解不同类型的用户、他们的目标和痛点。这会让你了解某些技术决策背后的宝贵背景。

Reviewing available documentation

After talking to stakeholders, the next step on the path to understanding a codebase is to comb through any and all available documentation, including ADRs. With a high-level understanding of the project itself, some of this documentation should start to make some sense. At this point, you are trying to learn as much about the codebase as you can through the documentation.

和利益相关者谈过之后，理解代码库的下一步是梳理所有可用文档，包括 ADR（架构决策记录）。有了对项目本身的高层理解，这些文档中的一部分应该开始讲得通了。此时你要做的，是通过文档尽可能多地了解代码库。

A big part of this is the infamous “onboarding documentation” to a project. This will tell you everything you need to know to get this project up and running on your local machine. This documentation has gotten better over the years with tools like Docker, but a review can still be a tedious process.

其中很大一块是那个声名在外的项目“入职文档”。它会告诉你在本机上把项目跑起来所需知道的一切。这些年有了 Docker 之类的工具，这种文档已经好多了，但通读一遍仍可能是个枯燥的过程。

While your job is not to write documentation at this point because you’re still getting familiar with everything, you should be taking notes and identifying gaps in the documentation. This will be something you can come back to later and fix and is a great way to contribute to the team.

虽然此刻你的工作不是写文档（因为你还在熟悉一切），但你应当做笔记、找出文档中的缺口。这些缺口日后可以回来补上，这也是你为团队做贡献的好方式。

The Documentation Trap
文档陷阱

Dan here. I once spent three days trying to understand a complex authentication system, carefully reading through what I thought was up-to-date documentation. When I finally asked a teammate for help, they laughed and said, “Oh, that documentation is from two versions ago. We completely rewrote the auth system last year.” The lesson? Documentation can lie, but the code never does. Always verify what you read against what’s actually running. And don’t be afraid to ask for help. A three-minute conversation would have saved me three days.
我是 Dan。有一次我花了三天试图理解一个复杂的认证系统，仔细读着我以为是最新的文档。最后我找同事求助，他笑了说：“哦，那文档是两个版本之前的。我们去年把认证系统整个重写了。”教训是什么？文档会说谎，但代码永远不会。一定要把你读到的和实际运行的对一遍。还有，别害怕求助。一次三分钟的对话本可以省我三天。

Understanding architecture and project structure

After understanding the overall project and reading through all of the available documentation, it’s time to examine the architecture and organization of the codebase. This is an important step before diving in and reading any code or configuration or writing code. The project’s structure can reveal a lot of information and give you a more holistic view of the project that will help you when navigating the codebase.

理解了项目全貌、读完所有可用文档之后，是时候考察代码库的架构和组织方式了。在一头扎进去读任何代码、配置或写代码之前，这是重要一步。项目结构能揭示大量信息，给你一个更整体的项目视图，在你导航代码库时帮上忙。

Most projects follow some form of architectural pattern, whether by deliberate design or through organic evolution. Start by identifying which pattern (or combination of patterns) the codebase follows.

大多数项目都遵循某种架构模式，无论是刻意设计还是自然演化而来。先识别代码库遵循哪种模式（或哪几种模式的组合）。

原书第 117 页

Package by layer organizes code horizontally based on technical responsibilities. You’ll often see top-level directories like controllers, services, repositories, and models. This approach groups similar technical components together, making it easy to find all components of a particular type. The following code is packaged by layer:

按层分包根据技术职责横向组织代码。你常会看到 controllers、services、repositories、models 这样的顶层目录。这种方式把同类技术组件归在一起，方便找到某一类型的所有组件。下面的代码就是按层分包的：

src/
  ├── controllers/
  │   ├── UserController.java
  │   └── ProductController.java
  ├── services/
  │   ├── UserService.java
  │   └── ProductService.java
  ├── repositories/
  │   ├── UserRepository.java
  │   └── ProductRepository.java
  └── models/
      ├── User.java
      └── Product.java

Package by feature organizes code vertically around business capabilities or features. You’ll see top-level directories representing business domains like users, products, and orders. This approach encapsulates all aspects of a feature together, making it easier to understand complete business workflows. The following is an example of code packaged by feature:

按特性分包围绕业务能力或特性纵向组织代码。你会看到代表业务域的顶层目录，如 users、products、orders。这种方式把一个特性的所有方面封装在一起，更容易理解完整的业务流程。下面是按特性分包的例子：

src/
  ├── users/
  │   ├── UserController.java
  │   ├── UserService.java
  │   ├── UserRepository.java
  │   └── User.java
  └── products/
      ├── ProductController.java
      ├── ProductService.java
      ├── ProductRepository.java
      └── Product.java

Hexagonal architecture (also known as ports and adapters) organizes code to separate business logic from external concerns. Look for a core domain model surrounded by adapters that connect to the outside world. This pattern emphasizes isolation of business rules from technical implementations. The following is an example of code that has a hexagonal architecture:

六边形架构（也称端口与适配器）组织代码，把业务逻辑与外部关注点分离。找一个核心领域模型，周围环绕着连接外部世界的适配器。这种模式强调业务规则与技术实现的隔离。下面是六边形架构代码的例子：

src/
  ├── domain/                  // Business logic
  │   ├── model/
  │   └── service/
  ├── application/             // Use cases, orchestration
  │   └── service/
  ├── ports/                   // Interfaces for adapters
  │   ├── input/
  │   └── output/
  └── adapters/                // Technical implementations
      ├── web/
      ├── persistence/
      └── messaging/

Microservices architecture splits functionality into multiple independent services. If you’re working in a microservices environment, you’ll need to understand both the architecture of your specific service and how it fits into the larger ecosystem. In the following example, each top-level service like user-service is its own microservice:

微服务架构把功能拆成多个独立服务。如果你在微服务环境工作，你既需要理解自己那个服务的架构，也要理解它如何嵌入更大的生态。在下面的例子中，每个像 user-service 这样的顶层服务就是一个独立微服务：

microservices-system/

    └── utils/

Understand the Execution Flow

Execution flow is the sequential path of instructions that a program follows during runtime, including all decisions, loops, and function calls that determine which code executes and in what order.

执行流是程序在运行时按顺序走过的指令路径，包括所有决定执行哪段代码、以什么顺序执行的判断、循环和函数调用。

Now that you have the big picture of the project and understand its purpose, you can begin looking at code. We aren’t actually writing any code or doing any in-depth analysis at this point; we are just trying to understand how the code flows. In this section, you will learn techniques for understanding the execution flow by finding application entry points, tracing requests and responses, and learning how to locate external dependencies.

既然你有了项目全局、理解了它的目的，就可以开始看代码了。此刻我们并不真的写代码或做深入分析，只是想理解代码如何流转。在本节中，你将学习通过找应用入口、跟踪请求和响应、以及定位外部依赖来理解执行流的技巧。

原书第 119 页

Finding application entry points

An application has a set of doors that act as entry points into your application. These doors come in the form of an application’s main method, public APIs, web UIs, and more. These doorways into the application are a great place to start if you want to learn about the different execution flows in an application.

一个应用有一组“门”，作为进入应用的入口。这些门表现为应用的 main 方法、公共 API、Web UI 等形式。如果你想了解应用中不同的执行流，这些通向应用的门道是绝佳的起点。

For example, in a Spring Boot web application,1 you can find the main class by looking for the @SpringBootApplication annotation and locating the main method:

例如，在一个 Spring Boot Web 应用中，1你可以通过查找 @SpringBootApplication 注解、定位 main 方法来找到主类：

1 We’ll be using the Spring PetClinic app for examples throughout this chapter. Even if you aren’t an expert in Java or Spring, it should be fairly straightforward to understand.
本章通篇使用 Spring PetClinic 应用作为例子。即使你不是 Java 或 Spring 专家，也应该相当容易理解。
@SpringBootApplication
public class PetClinicApplication {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        SpringApplication.run(PetClinicApplication.class, args);
    }
}

When you have identified one of the application’s entry points, you can begin to follow the code’s execution flow. This is where using your IDE’s debugger can be a really valuable tool. Set a breakpoint on the run method and then use the step-through functionality. This will give you insight into what the framework is doing under the hood and provides an excellent starting point for understanding the codebase.

当你识别出应用的一个入口，就可以开始跟随代码的执行流了。这时使用 IDE 的调试器会是一个非常有价值的工具。在 run 方法上设个断点，然后用单步执行功能。这会让你洞察框架在幕后做什么，为理解代码库提供绝佳起点。

To learn more about the application’s entry points, you can locate the public APIs, which in this PetClinic example application are the REST endpoints. The following @GetMapping section tells us that we can send a request to /pets/new and that this is the method that will execute. Now we can use the features of the IDE and our debugging tools to follow the execution path:

要更多了解应用的入口，你可以定位公共 API，在这个 PetClinic 例子里就是 REST 端点。下面的 @GetMapping 告诉我们可以向 /pets/new 发请求，而这就是将被执行的方法。现在我们可以用 IDE 的功能和调试工具跟随执行路径：

@GetMapping("/pets/new")
public String initCreationForm(Owner owner, ModelMap model) {
   Pet pet = new Pet();
   owner.addPet(pet);
   return VIEWS_PETS_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FORM;
}

There are many entry points that can help you map out the execution flow of an application. Here are some common ones, but there are many more:

有许多入口可以帮你勾勒应用的执行流。下面是一些常见的，但还有更多：

  • Main/bootstrap methods — the traditional starting point of execution (like Java’s main()).main/引导方法——传统的执行起点（如 Java 的 main()）。
  • Public APIs/controllers — endpoints that expose functionality to external systems.公共 API/控制器——向外部系统暴露功能的端点。
  • Event handlers/listeners — code that executes in response to specific events or triggers.事件处理器/监听器——响应特定事件或触发器而执行的代码。
  • Scheduled tasks/jobs — functionality that runs at predetermined intervals.定时任务/作业——按预定间隔运行的功能。
  • Lifecycle hooks — methods called during component creation, startup, or shutdown.生命周期钩子——在组件创建、启动或关闭期间被调用的方法。
  • Plug-in/extension points — interfaces designed for extending application functionality.插件/扩展点——为扩展应用功能而设计的接口。
  • Message consumers — code that responds to messages from queues or message brokers.消息消费者——响应来自队列或消息代理的消息的代码。
  • Command-line argument processors — logic that handles startup parameters.命令行参数处理器——处理启动参数的逻辑。
  • Database triggers/stored procedures — server-side code that executes in response to data changes.数据库触发器/存储过程——响应数据变更而执行的服务端代码。

The key is knowing how to find the right doors to open. When you have identified them, you can use them as entryways into understanding the flow of an application.

关键是知道怎么找到该推开的门。一旦识别出它们，你就可以把它们当作理解应用流程的入口。

Following the data: Tracing request journeys

When working with existing codebases, especially web applications and APIs (REST, GraphQL, gRPC), tracing the journey of a request through a system is a great way to understand how the code works and the systems involved. While documentation or tests might tell you what is supposed to happen, following a request will reveal what actually happens.

在既有代码库上工作时，尤其是 Web 应用和 API（REST、GraphQL、gRPC），跟踪一个请求穿过系统的旅程，是理解代码如何工作、涉及哪些系统的好办法。文档或测试可能告诉你应该发生什么，而跟踪一个请求会揭示实际发生什么。

Request tracing is valuable because it does the following:

请求跟踪之所以有价值，是因为它：

  • Reveals the actual path of execution through multiple components and systems揭示跨多个组件和系统的真实执行路径
  • Helps identify all the involved layers (controllers, services, repositories, etc.)帮你识别所有涉及的层（控制器、服务、仓库等）
  • Exposes data transformations that happen along the way暴露沿途发生的数据转换
  • Uncovers hidden business logic and validation rules揭示隐藏的业务逻辑和校验规则
  • Shows how errors are handled in practice展示错误在实际中如何处理

As a developer exploring a new codebase, some really great tools are at your disposal for tracing requests. In this section, you’ll learn about a few of these tools. You might not need to use all of them, but knowing what is available is helpful. Try a few of them out and see what tools work well for you in your workflow.

作为一个探索新代码库的开发者，你手头有一些非常棒的请求跟踪工具。本节你会了解其中几个。你可能不需要全都用，但知道有哪些可用是有帮助的。试几个，看看哪些工具在你的工作流里顺手。

Browser developer tools. When working with web applications, browser developer tools are a good first place to inspect a request and response. In the following example, we are running the PetClinic application and adding a new pet to an owner (Figure 6-1).

浏览器开发者工具。处理 Web 应用时，浏览器开发者工具是检查请求和响应的好起点。在下面的例子中，我们运行 PetClinic 应用，给一位主人添加一只新宠物（图 6-1）。

原书第 121 页

When you fill out the form and click the Add Pet button, it will send a request to the following endpoint:

当你填好表单、点击 Add Pet 按钮，它会向下面这个端点发送请求：

@PostMapping("/pets/new")
public String processCreationForm(Owner owner, @Valid Pet pet,
BindingResult result, RedirectAttributes redirectAttributes) {

   if (StringUtils.hasText(pet.getName()) && pet.isNew() &&
   owner.getPet(pet.getName(), true) != null)
      result.rejectValue("name", "duplicate", "already exists");

   LocalDate currentDate = LocalDate.now();
   if (pet.getBirthDate() != null && pet.getBirthDate().isAfter(currentDate)) {
      result.rejectValue("birthDate", "typeMismatch.birthDate");
   }

   if (result.hasErrors()) {
      return VIEWS_PETS_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FORM;
   }
原书第 122 页
   owner.addPet(pet);
   this.owners.save(owner);
   redirectAttributes.addFlashAttribute("message", "New Pet has been Added");
   return "redirect:/owners/{ownerId}";
}

If you open up the developer tools and inspect the Network tab, you will see the POST request to the /pets/new endpoint where you can examine the headers, payload, response, and more, as shown in Figure 6-2.

如果你打开开发者工具、查看 Network 标签页，会看到发往 /pets/new 端点的 POST 请求，可以在其中检查请求头、载荷、响应等，如图 6-2 所示。

API testing tools. If you want to test an API endpoint directly and it’s a simple GET request, you can put the URL in your browser and see the result. When it’s any other request method like POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, you will need to reach for an API testing tool. There are some really great tools on the market like Postman, Insomnia, and Bruno. You will also find plug-ins for a lot of the major IDEs out there that contain similar functionality.

API 测试工具。如果你想直接测试一个 API 端点，而它是个简单的 GET 请求，你可以把 URL 贴进浏览器看结果。当请求方法是 POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE 之类时，你就需要动用 API 测试工具。市面上有 Postman、Insomnia、Bruno 等很棒的工具。你还会在很多主流 IDE 里找到带类似功能的插件。

In the previous section, we submitted the form from the browser and used developer tools to inspect the POST request under the hood. What if you didn’t want to go through the UI and test the API endpoint directly? This is where API testing tools shine, giving you the ability to send a POST request along with headers, authorization, a request body, and more. After sending the request, you then have the ability to inspect the response, allowing you to bypass the UI altogether (Figure 6-3).

上一节我们从浏览器提交表单、用开发者工具查看幕后的 POST 请求。如果你不想经过 UI、而是直接测试 API 端点呢？这就是 API 测试工具大放异彩的地方：它让你能带上请求头、授权、请求体等发送 POST 请求。发送请求后，你还能检查响应，从而完全绕过 UI（图 6-3）。

原书第 123 页

You can test this endpoint with a tool like Postman and examine the following:

你可以用 Postman 这样的工具测试这个端点，并检查以下各项：

  • Required fields and data types — identify which fields are mandatory in the request body and what format they expect (strings, numbers, arrays, etc.).必填字段和数据类型——识别请求体中哪些字段是必填的、它们期望什么格式（字符串、数字、数组等）。
  • Input validation behavior — test how the API handles invalid data, missing fields, malformed JSON, and edge cases like empty strings or null values.输入校验行为——测试 API 如何处理无效数据、缺失字段、畸形 JSON，以及空字符串或 null 值之类的边界情况。
  • Authentication and authorization — verify that protected endpoints properly reject unauthorized requests and accept valid credentials.认证和授权——验证受保护端点是否正确拒绝未授权请求、接受有效凭证。
  • Response structure and status codes — examine what data is returned on successful requests versus different types of failures (400, 401, 404, 500, etc.).响应结构和状态码——检查成功请求返回什么数据，以及不同类型失败（400、401、404、500 等）时返回什么。
  • Error message quality — assess whether error responses provide clear, actionable feedback for debugging.错误信息质量——评估错误响应是否提供清晰、可操作的调试反馈。
  • Performance characteristics — measure response times and identify any endpoints that are unusually slow.性能特征——测量响应时间，找出异常缓慢的端点。

Logging. Logs provide insight into the system’s internal behavior. In many applications, logs might be the only tool available for debugging issues or tracing the journey of a request in production. When examining the code, look for logging statements like this:

日志。日志让你洞察系统的内部行为。在许多应用中，日志可能是生产环境里调试问题或跟踪请求旅程唯一可用的工具。阅读代码时，寻找这样的日志语句：

log.info("Finding owner with id: {}", ownerId);

The following endpoint will list out all the pets for a particular owner. If you make a request to this endpoint with a valid owner ID, you will see two new lines in the log (Figure 6-4). You will also notice that the curly braces are replaced with the actual values:

下面这个端点会列出某位主人的所有宠物。如果你用一个有效的主人 ID 请求这个端点，会在日志里看到两行新内容（图 6-4）。你还会注意到花括号被替换成了实际值：

@GetMapping("/owners/{id}/pets")
public List<Pet> findAllPets(@PathVariable("id") int ownerId) {
   log.info("Finding owner with id: {}", ownerId);
   Optional<Owner> owner = ownerRepository.findById(ownerId);
   if (owner.isPresent()) {
      var pets = owner.get().getPets();
      log.info("Found {} pets for owner", pets.size());
      return pets;
   }
   return null;
}

@PostMapping("/pets/new")
public String processCreationForm(Owner owner, @Valid Pet pet,
BindingResult result, RedirectAttributes redirectAttributes) {

   // Set breakpoint here
   if (StringUtils.hasText(pet.getName()) && pet.isNew()

   && owner.getPet(pet.getName(), true) != null)
      result.rejectValue("name", "duplicate", "already exists");

   // Additional validation...
}

You know that the application is rejecting a value for a new pet, but why? This conditional has multiple parts that all need to be true for a duplicate name error to occur. By setting a breakpoint on this line, you can step through and examine the following (Figure 6-5):

你知道应用在拒绝新宠物的某个值，但为什么？这个条件有多个部分，只有全部为真才会出现重名错误。在这一行设断点，你可以单步执行并检查以下内容（图 6-5）：

  • What each condition evaluates to — does StringUtils.hasText(pet.getName()) return true? Is pet.isNew() true?每个条件的求值结果——StringUtils.hasText(pet.getName()) 返回 true 吗？pet.isNew() 为真吗？

When you use debugging tools in your IDE to step through complex business logic, the debugger reveals not just what path the code takes, but why it takes that path. This is especially valuable when behavior doesn’t match your expectations. For instance, if logs indicate that a pet name already exists but you’re certain that’s incorrect, the debugger allows you to verify this directly.

当你用 IDE 的调试工具单步走过复杂业务逻辑时，调试器不仅揭示代码走了哪条路，还揭示为什么走这条路。当行为不符合你的预期时，这一点尤其有价值。例如，如果日志显示一个宠物名已存在、而你确信这不对，调试器让你直接验证这一点。

Locating external dependencies

Rarely will you find an application that runs in isolation. Modern applications depend on external services in the form of public APIs and internal services that they communicate with. An important part of understanding the execution flow is locating any and all of the external dependencies your application communicates with. This could be in the form of other APIs, databases, caches, and more.

你很少能找到一个孤立运行的应用。现代应用以公共 API 和内部服务的形式依赖外部服务。理解执行流的一个重要部分，是定位你的应用与之通信的所有外部依赖。它们可能是其他 API、数据库、缓存等形式。

Without a complete understanding of the entire application, how will you locate these dependencies? A really good place to start is by examining configuration files. In our PetClinic application that is built on Spring Boot, you can look at the application.properties or application.yaml configuration to see what dependencies are declared. In the following example, you can see that this application depends on a PostgreSQL database, an external service, and an email host:

在没有完整理解整个应用的情况下，你怎么定位这些依赖？一个非常好的起点是检查配置文件。在我们基于 Spring Boot 的 PetClinic 应用中，你可以看 application.properties 或 application.yaml 配置，了解声明了哪些依赖。在下面的例子中，你可以看到这个应用依赖一个 PostgreSQL 数据库、一个外部服务和一个邮件主机：

# database
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:postgresql://db-server:5432/petclinic
spring.datasource.driver-class-name=org.postgresql.Driver
# external service
payment.service.endpoint=https://payments.example.com/api/v2
# email host
email.service.host=smtp.company.com

For containerized applications, check Docker Compose files or Kubernetes manifests to identify linked services:

对于容器化应用，检查 Docker Compose 文件或 Kubernetes 清单来识别关联的服务：

# In docker-compose.yml
services:
  app:
    image: petclinic:latest
    depends_on:
      - mysql
      - redis
      - kafka

Locating internal frameworks and libraries

One of the biggest challenges in exploring existing codebases is encountering internal or homegrown frameworks and libraries. These are custom solutions built in-house to solve specific business problems or technical challenges. While they might have been the right decision at the time of creation, they often present unique obstacles for new team members trying to explore and modify the codebase.

探索既有代码库时最大的挑战之一，就是遇到内部或自研的框架和库。这些是为解决特定业务问题或技术挑战而在内部构建的定制方案。虽然在创建时它们可能是正确决策，但它们常常给试图探索和修改代码库的新成员带来独特障碍。

Why would a team decide to build something internally versus going with an external solution? Internal frameworks typically emerge for several reasons:

为什么一个团队会决定内部自研，而不是用外部方案？内部框架通常因以下几个原因出现：

  • The original team needed functionality that wasn’t available in existing libraries.最初的团队需要现有库中没有的功能。
  • They had specific security or performance requirements.他们有特定的安全或性能要求。
  • The total cost of bringing in an external solution was too high.引入外部方案的总成本太高。
  • They built something to quickly solve a problem that evolved over time.他们为快速解决一个问题而造了东西，而那个问题随时间演化了。
  • They didn’t know a solution existed or didn’t fully understand it.他们不知道已有方案存在，或没有完全理解它。
Meta work is more interesting than real work.
——Neal Ford, director and software architect at Thoughtworks

元工作比真正的工作更有趣。
——Neal Ford，Thoughtworks 总监兼软件架构师

Unfortunately, these solutions often suffer from poor documentation, lack of access to the original developers, and inconsistent maintenance.

不幸的是，这些方案常常文档糟糕、找不到原开发者、维护也时断时续。

Identifying internal frameworks. Internal frameworks can be harder to spot than external dependencies because they’re embedded directly in the codebase. Here are the key indicators you’re dealing with a homegrown solution:

识别内部框架。内部框架比外部依赖更难发现，因为它们直接嵌在代码库里。以下是你正在面对自研方案的关键信号：

  • Package naming patterns — look for packages with company-specific prefixes or generic names like com.yourcompany.framework, utils.common.core, or internal.shared.包命名模式——寻找带公司特定前缀或泛名的包，如 com.yourcompany.framework、utils.common.core 或 internal.shared。
  • Custom base classes — many classes extending from custom base classes with names like BaseService, AbstractController, or CommonEntity indicate framework code.自定义基类——许多类继承自 BaseService、AbstractController、CommonEntity 之类命名的自定义基类，表明是框架代码。
  • Custom annotations — nonstandard annotations that aren’t part of popular frameworks often signal internal solutions:自定义注解——不属于流行框架的非标准注解常常标志着内部方案：
@Entity
@CompanyTable(name = "users", audit = true)
public class User extends BaseCompanyEntity {

    @CompanyField(encrypted = true)
    private String email;
}
  • Utility classes with broad scope — classes named AppUtils, BusinessHelper, or SystemManager that handle diverse responsibilities across the application often.职责宽泛的工具类——名为 AppUtils、BusinessHelper 或 SystemManager、在应用中承担五花八门职责的类。
  • Heavy configuration — extensive custom YAML/XML files or configuration classes that don’t match standard library patterns.繁重配置——大量不符合标准库模式的自定义 YAML/XML 文件或配置类。
原书第 128 页

Working with internal frameworks. The following tips will help you explore internal frameworks and leave the code in a better place than you found it:

使用内部框架。以下技巧帮你探索内部框架，并让代码比你发现它时更好：

  • Find usage examples first — search the codebase for how other developers use the framework. Real examples are often more instructive than documentation.先找使用示例——在代码库中搜索其他开发者如何使用这个框架。真实示例往往比文档更有指导意义。
  • Look for tests — framework code sometimes has better test coverage since it needs to work across multiple scenarios. Tests reveal intended behavior and edge cases.寻找测试——框架代码有时测试覆盖更好，因为它需要跨多种场景工作。测试揭示预期行为和边界情况。
  • Document as you learn — create notes about what the framework does and how to use it. Even basic documentation helps future developers.边学边写文档——记下这个框架做什么、怎么用。哪怕是基础文档也能帮助后来的开发者。
  • Check version control history — use git blame and commit messages to understand why the framework was built and how it evolved.查看版本控制历史——用 git blame 和提交信息理解为什么建这个框架、它如何演化。
  • Evaluate the trade-offs — consider whether the framework still provides value or is becoming a maintenance burden. Sometimes replacing internal solutions with standard libraries is the right long-term choice.权衡利弊——考虑这个框架是否仍在提供价值，还是正在变成维护负担。有时用标准库替换内部方案才是正确的长期选择。
  • Make incremental improvements — apply the scout rule (more on this later in the chapter) by improving naming, adding documentation, or enhancing test coverage as you work with the framework.做渐进式改进——在使用框架时应用童子军规则（本章后面详述）：改进命名、补充文档或增强测试覆盖。

Build Mental Models Incrementally

A mental model is your internal representation of how the system works, and developing a robust model takes time and deliberate practice. If you’re going to build a mental model of a system, it’s much easier to do if you break down the system incrementally. Instead of trying to build a mental model of an entire ecommerce application, take a single path like the checkout process and build from there. It’s also helpful to avoid letting tools or perfectionism get in the way. Often, a simple hand-drawn model on a scratch pad will suffice.

心智模型是你对系统如何工作的内部表征，而建立一个健壮的模型需要时间和刻意练习。如果你要为一个系统建立心智模型，把系统渐进拆解会容易得多。不要试图为整个电商应用一下子建立心智模型，而是拿一条路径（如结账流程）从那里开始构建。另外，别让工具或完美主义成为障碍，这也有帮助。很多时候，便签纸上一张简单手绘模型就够了。

In this section, you will learn some practical methods for building mental models such as breaking complex systems into smaller ones, visualizing those models, and gradually expanding your knowledge.

在本节中，你将学习一些建立心智模型的实用方法，比如把复杂系统拆小、把模型可视化，以及逐步扩展你的知识。

AI 提示

Another benefit these days of text-based diagramming is that generative AI can help you with an initial draft that you can refine further manually. You can describe your system or process to an AI tool and ask it to generate Mermaid syntax, then iterate on the output to match your specific needs.
如今基于文本画图的另一个好处是：生成式 AI 可以帮你出初稿，你再手动精修。你可以向 AI 工具描述你的系统或流程，让它生成 Mermaid 语法，然后根据你的具体需求迭代输出。

Breaking down complex systems

Breaking down complex systems is an important part of building mental models. When you join a new project with a large codebase, trying to understand everything at once is overwhelming and inefficient. Instead, you should focus on breaking complex systems into manageable pieces.

拆解复杂系统是建立心智模型的重要一环。当你加入一个代码库庞大的新项目时，试图一次性理解一切既让人崩溃又低效。相反，你应当专注于把复杂系统拆成可管理的小块。

You learned about application entry points in a previous section, and this is a great place to start. For example, in an ecommerce application, you might have defined some of these execution flows:

你在前面小节学过应用入口，那是很好的起点。例如，在一个电商应用中，你可能会定义这样一些执行流：

  • New customer flow — a new user signs up, becomes a customer, and receives a promotional coupon.新客户流程——新用户注册、成为客户、收到一张促销优惠券。
  • Checkout flow — what happens when a user completes a purchase with products in their cart.结账流程——当用户用购物车里的商品完成购买时会发生什么。
  • Product review flow — a customer provides feedback on a purchased product.商品评价流程——客户对购买的商品给出反馈。

These are great examples of breaking a complex system into smaller manageable pieces that you can wrap your head around. Once you have seen how a new product review is recorded and you have seen the code associated with those steps, you can begin to build a mental model of this process. Everyone learns differently, and maybe you’re someone who wants to build a mental model around the code and not a process. If your application uses a package-by-feature arrangement, you could build models of each feature. In the following example, we can see all of the code associated with the cart feature:

这些就是把复杂系统拆成可理解小块的好例子。一旦你看过一条新商品评价是如何记录的、看过与这些步骤相关的代码，你就可以开始为这个过程建立心智模型。每个人学习方式不同，也许你是那种想围绕代码、而不是围绕流程建立心智模型的人。如果你的应用采用按特性分包的结构，你可以为每个特性建立模型。在下面的例子中，我们可以看到与购物车特性相关的所有代码：

│       └── CartItemDTO.java

Visualizing your mental models

Visualizing code relationships can help you build these mental models. In Chapter 4, you learned about software modeling and some of the types of diagrams at your disposal. Your visualizations do not need to be professional: they can range from simple sketches to full UML diagrams. Use whatever level of detail helps you understand the system. The first part of visualizing your mental model is to choose your visualization type. Different types of visualizations serve different purposes in software engineering:

把代码关系可视化能帮你建立这些心智模型。在第 4 章中，你学习了软件建模以及可用的一些图类型。你的可视化不需要很专业：从简单草图到完整 UML 图都可以。用任何能帮你理解系统的细节程度。可视化心智模型的第一步是选择可视化类型。在软件工程中，不同类型的可视化服务于不同目的：

  • Flowcharts — help you understand sequential processes and decision points流程图——帮你理解顺序流程和决策点
  • Entity–relationship diagrams — clarify data structures and their relationships实体—关系图——阐明数据结构及其关系
  • Sequence diagrams — illustrate how components interact over time时序图——展示组件随时间如何交互
  • Component diagrams — show the high-level architecture and dependencies组件图——展示高层架构和依赖
  • Mind maps — help organize related concepts hierarchically思维导图——帮你层次化地组织相关概念

You can begin by starting with a simple representation and add details as your comprehension of the system grows. For example, when visualizing the checkout flow in an ecommerce system, you might start with just the major components. 你可以先从简单的表示开始，随着对系统理解加深再添加细节。例如，在可视化电商系统的结账流程时，你可能先只画主要组件。下面是用 Mermaid 语法写的简单流程图，Mermaid 是一个流行的基于 Markdown 的画图工具：

graph TD
    A[Shopping Cart] --> B[Checkout Form]
    B --> C[Payment Processing]
    C --> D[Order Confirmation]

Gradually expanding your scope

Once you understand individual components, incrementally expand your focus to the larger system’s behavior:

一旦你理解了各个组件，渐进地把关注点扩展到更大系统的行为：

  1. Start with single methods in isolation.从孤立的单个方法开始。
  2. Move to classes and their direct dependencies.进到类及其直接依赖。
  3. Continue to feature-level flows that span multiple components.继续到跨多个组件的特性级流程。
  4. Finally, understand cross-cutting concerns like security or transaction handling.最后，理解横切关注点，如安全或事务处理。

This incremental approach prevents cognitive overload while building a comprehensive view of the system.

这种渐进方法在建立系统综合视图的同时，防止认知过载。

By investing time in building accurate mental models, you’ll make better decisions when modifying the codebase. Remember that this is an ongoing process and takes time. Even experienced team members continue refining their understanding of the system as a whole as it evolves. Now that you have learned how to understand unfamiliar codebases, let’s look at a sample process for working with existing code.

通过投入时间建立准确的心智模型，你在修改代码库时会做出更好的决策。记住这是一个持续的过程，需要时间。即使是经验丰富的团队成员，也会随着系统演进而不断完善对它整体的理解。既然你已经学会如何理解陌生代码库，我们来看一个在既有代码上工作的示例流程。

A Sample Process

Over time, you will develop a feel for working with existing code. However, it can help to have a process. Christopher Judd teaches the following method in his boot camps:

久而久之，你会对在既有代码上工作培养出手感。不过有个流程会有帮助。Christopher Judd 在他的训练营里教授以下方法：

  1. Clone the project from the source code management system.从源代码管理系统克隆项目。
  2. Review the README, coding standards, architecture, and other supporting documentation.阅读 README、编码规范、架构和其他支撑文档。
  3. Take notes (architecture, build commands, common SQL, industry standards, terms, etc.) as you go. Don’t be afraid to share these notes with your teammates!边做边记笔记（架构、构建命令、常用 SQL、行业标准、术语等）。别害怕和队友分享这些笔记！
  4. Review build scripts.阅读构建脚本。
  5. Review the project dependencies.查看项目依赖。
  6. Review the project structure (packages, namespaces, modules, artifacts, etc.).查看项目结构（包、命名空间、模块、制品等）。
  7. Review the CI/CD pipelines.查看 CI/CD 流水线。
  8. Install any project dependencies (build tools, runtimes, languages).安装项目依赖（构建工具、运行时、语言）。
  9. From your IDE: (a) run and debug the application; (b) add breakpoints to interesting methods, connecting them back to the running application; (c) run and debug unit tests; (d) add breakpoints to interesting methods, connecting them back to the running application.在 IDE 中：(a) 运行并调试应用；(b) 在感兴趣的方法上加断点，把它们连回正在运行的应用；(c) 运行并调试单元测试；(d) 在感兴趣的方法上加断点，连回正在运行的应用。
  10. From the command line: (a) build the project artifacts; (b) run the unit tests; (c) start any required containers (such as the datastore); (d) run the application locally (ports, URLs, etc.).在命令行：(a) 构建项目制品；(b) 运行单元测试；(c) 启动所需容器（如数据存储）；(d) 在本地运行应用（端口、URL 等）。

Remember that understanding an existing codebase is an iterative process. You won’t be able to comprehend everything on your first pass, and that is completely normal. Each time you work on an issue or a new feature, you will gain deeper knowledge.

记住，理解一个既有代码库是一个迭代过程。你第一遍不可能理解一切，这完全正常。每次你处理一个问题或一个新功能，都会获得更深的认识。

Making Changes Safely

Now that you have some tips and a process for understanding an existing codebase, it’s time to learn how to safely modify one. Existing systems have likely gone through numerous iterations, features, and more. You can’t just run into the ring like a wild boxer swinging away and expending all of your energy in the first round. You need to navigate the codebase methodically and be careful that you don’t break things. You have likely heard the phrase “move fast and break things,” and that might have a place in certain scenarios, but this is not one of them.

既然你有了理解既有代码库的技巧和流程，是时候学习如何安全地修改它了。既有系统很可能已经历了无数次迭代、功能增删等。你不能像个 wild boxer 那样冲进拳台、第一回合就把体力挥光。你需要有条不紊地导航代码库，小心别搞坏东西。你可能听过“快速行动、打破陈规”这句话，它在某些场景下有一席之地，但这里不是。

原书第 134 页

Refactoring Safely

When working with legacy systems and existing codebases, there is often potential for refactoring code to improve readability, performance, and more. In this situation, you want to make sure you have a plan and don’t try to do too much at once.

在遗留系统和既有代码库上工作时，常常有重构代码以改善可读性、性能等的空间。在这种情况下，你要确保有计划，别想一次做太多。

Rely on existing tests

As you learned in the previous section, tests play a big role in understanding a codebase, but they also make your job of refactoring code safer and easier. If the project has a comprehensive suite of tests, you’ll want to lean on them heavily. Tests serve as your safety net, allowing you to make small changes, run the tests, and ensure that you haven’t affected something elsewhere in the project.

正如你在上一节学到的，测试在理解代码库方面作用很大，但它们也让你重构代码的工作更安全、更轻松。如果项目有一套全面的测试，你要狠狠依靠它们。测试充当你的安全网，让你做小改动、跑测试、确认没有影响项目别处。

In the following example. you are refactoring the calculateTotal method to separate out the calculation of the subtotal and application of a discount. When refactoring, you should avoid modifying the tests since the goal is to improve the code structure while preserving its behavior. After each step of this refactor, you should run the tests associated with this method to ensure that behavior remains unchanged:

在下面的例子中，你在重构 calculateTotal 方法，把小计计算和折扣应用分离开。重构时你应当避免修改测试，因为目标是在保持行为不变的前提下改善代码结构。在这次重构的每一步之后，你都应当运行与该方法相关的测试，确保行为不变：

// Before refactoring
public double calculateTotal(Order order) {
    double total = 0;
    for (OrderItem item : order.getItems()) {
        total += item.getPrice() * item.getQuantity();
    }
    if (order.hasDiscount()) {
        total = total * (1 - order.getDiscountRate());
    }
    return total;
}

// After refactoring
public double calculateTotal(Order order) {
    double subtotal = calculateSubtotal(order);
    return applyDiscount(subtotal, order);
}

private double calculateSubtotal(Order order) {
    return order.getItems().stream()
        .mapToDouble(item -> item.getPrice() * item.getQuantity())
        .sum();
}

private double applyDiscount(double amount, Order order) {
    return order.hasDiscount()
        ? amount * (1 - order.getDiscountRate())
        : amount;
}

Add tests before refactoring

In the previous example, we leaned on the tests to ensure that nothing else was affected in the larger scope of the project. If the application doesn’t have adequate test coverage on the changes you’re proposing, this is your chance to add tests before refactoring any existing code. This approach, sometimes called test-driven refactoring, follows these steps:

上一个例子中，我们依靠测试确保项目更大范围内没有别的东西受影响。如果应用对你提议的改动没有足够测试覆盖，这就是你在重构任何既有代码之前补测试的机会。这种方式有时被称为测试驱动重构，遵循以下步骤：

  1. Write tests that document the current behavior.编写记录当前行为的测试。
  2. Verify that tests pass with the current implementation.验证测试在当前实现下通过。
  3. Refactor the code.重构代码。
  4. Verify that tests still pass with the new implementation.验证测试在新实现下仍然通过。

The following unit test verifies that the order service correctly applies a 10% discount when calculating the total for an order that qualifies for discounting:

下面的单元测试验证：当计算一张符合折扣条件的订单的总价时，订单服务正确地应用了 10% 折扣：

@Test
public void calculateTotalAppliesDiscountWhenOrderHasDiscount() {
    // Given
    OrderItem item1 = new OrderItem("Product1", 10.0, 2);
    OrderItem item2 = new OrderItem("Product2", 15.0, 1);
    Order order = new Order(Arrays.asList(item1, item2), true, 0.1);

    // When
    double total = orderService.calculateTotal(order);

    // Then
    assertEquals(31.5, total, 0.001); // (10*2 + 15*1) * 0.9 = 31.5
}

Adding tests like this before making changes helps you understand the existing behavior and gives you confidence that your refactoring preserves that behavior.

在改动前补这样的测试，帮你理解既有行为，并让你确信重构保持了该行为。

It’s important to remember that when adding tests to existing codebases, your first goal is to document the existing behavior, not change it. Even if you know of a better way to refactor the code or fix something that you are sure is a bug, you should first write the tests to confirm the current behavior. You can then come back and address bugs or additional refactoring after your tests are in place.

重要的是记住：向既有代码库补测试时，你的首要目标是记录既有行为，而不是改变它。即使你知道有更好的重构方式、或确信某处是个 bug，也应当先写测试确认当前行为。等测试就位后，你再回头处理 bug 或做额外重构。

The Scout Rule

The scout rule is a principle in software development that states: “Always leave the code better than you found it.” It’s inspired by the camping philosophy from the Boy Scouts of America, where scouts are taught to leave a campsite cleaner than they found it.

童子军规则是软件开发中的一条原则：“永远让代码比你发现它时更好。”它灵感来自美国童子军的露营哲学，即教导童子军离开营地时要比来时更干净。

原书第 136 页

The scout rule encourages making small, incremental improvements to code quality whenever you touch a file. These improvements might include the following:

童子军规则鼓励你每次碰一个文件时，都对代码质量做一点小的渐进式改进。这些改进可能包括：

  • Adding missing documentation补充缺失的文档
  • Improving variable or method names for clarity改善变量或方法名以提升清晰度
  • Breaking down overly complex methods拆解过于复杂的方法
  • Removing dead code移除死代码
  • Fixing minor bugs you discover修复你发现的小 bug

In the following example, simply by improving the method name, adding type parameters, using an enhanced for loop, and adding documentation, you’ve made the code significantly more maintainable without changing its core functionality:

在下面的例子中，仅仅通过改进方法名、加上类型参数、使用增强 for 循环、补上文档，你就让代码的可维护性大幅提升，而没有改变其核心功能：

// Before applying the Scout Rule
public void prcs(List l) {
    for (int i = 0; i < l.size(); i++) {
        Object o = l.get(i);
        // Process object
        // ...
    }
}

// After applying the Scout Rule
/**
 * Processes a list of customer records and updates their status in the database.
 *
 * @param customers The list of customers to process
 */
public void processCustomers(List<Customer> customers) {
    for (Customer customer : customers) {
        // Process customer
        // ...
    }
}

While the scout rule encourages you to clean up code as you go, you need to find a balance between cleanup and the task at hand. In larger codebases, you could spend all your time simply improving code, only to realize you haven’t fixed what you originally set out to fix.

虽然童子军规则鼓励你顺手清理代码，但你需要在清理和手头任务之间找到平衡。在较大的代码库里，你可能把所有时间都花在改进代码上，结果发现最初要修的东西还没修。

Not all code that could be improved should be improved immediately. Consider these factors when deciding whether to refactor.

并非所有可以改进的代码都应当立刻改进。决定是否重构时，考虑以下因素。

You can refactor code in these circumstances:

在这些情况下你可以重构代码：

  • The code you’re working on is difficult to understand.你正在改的代码难以理解。
  • You need to add a feature to the area.你需要在该区域加一个功能。
原书第 137 页
  • You’re fixing a bug in the code.你在修这段代码里的一个 bug。
  • The code is causing performance issues.这段代码正在导致性能问题。
  • Multiple developers frequently work in this area.多位开发者频繁在这个区域工作。

You should consider deferring refactoring in these cases:

在这些情况下，你应当考虑推迟重构：

  • The code works fine and rarely needs changes.代码工作良好，很少需要改动。
  • You’re under tight deadline pressure.你面临紧迫的截止日期压力。
  • The risk of breaking the code outweighs the benefits.搞坏代码的风险大于收益。
  • The refactoring would require extensive changes beyond your current task.重构需要超出你当前任务的大量改动。
  • You don’t have adequate test coverage to ensure safety.你没有足够测试覆盖来确保安全。

Small, Reversible Changes

Making incremental, easily reversible changes is the safest way to modify existing code without affecting the entire system. This is a skill you’ll need to continually practice to master. While you might be tempted to tackle complex problems all at once, and product owners might push for bigger, more impactful changes, your goal should be to make smaller modifications that don’t disrupt the system as a whole.

做渐进式、易回滚的小改动，是在不影响整个系统的前提下修改既有代码最安全的方式。这是一项你需要不断练习才能掌握的技能。虽然你可能忍不住想一口气解决复杂问题，产品负责人也可能推动更大、更有冲击力的改动，但你的目标应当是做不扰乱系统整体的较小修改。

Change management strategies

A change management strategy for software teams is a structured approach to handling modifications in your applications. It’s essentially a system for proposing, reviewing, implementing, and tracking changes to maintain code quality and team alignment. When aligning with small, reversible changes, your change management strategy should prioritize safety and visibility.

软件团队的变更管理策略，是一种处理应用修改的结构化方法。它本质上是一个提出、评审、实施和跟踪变更的系统，用于保持代码质量和团队一致。当与小而可逆的变更对齐时，你的变更管理策略应当把安全和可见性放在优先位置。

Here are some practical strategies you can use in your change management approach:

以下是你可以在变更管理中使用的一些实用策略：

  • Make changes visible — ensure that your changes are well-documented and easy to understand by others. This doesn’t need to be exhaustive and should explain what drove the change and how you implemented it.让变更可见——确保你的变更文档齐全、他人容易理解。不必面面俱到，但应解释是什么驱动了这个改动、你是怎么实现的。
  • Build in verification — include ways to verify that your changes work as expected. Verification methods for teams can include automated tests, code reviews, and static analysis.内建验证——包含验证变更按预期工作的方法。团队的验证方式可以包括自动化测试、代码评审和静态分析。
  • Plan for rollback — Murphy’s law states that what can go wrong will go wrong. Always have a plan to revert changes if problems arise. When you make smaller changes as we are proposing here, rolling them back should be easier.规划回滚——墨菲定律说：可能出错的终将出错。一定要有出问题时回退变更的计划。当你按我们这里建议做较小改动时，回滚也会更容易。
  • Monitor effects — watch for unexpected consequences of your changes. This is where having good observability into your applications really pays off.监控影响——警惕变更带来的意外后果。这时对你应用良好的可观测性就真正派上用场了。

Small, testable increments

Once you get into the mindset of working in smaller increments that you can test, your job of modifying existing codebases becomes less stressful and easier to manage. When you adopt this approach, you will see the following benefits:

一旦你进入“以可测试的小增量工作”的心态，修改既有代码库的工作就没那么大压力、也更容易管理。采用这种方式后，你会看到以下好处：

  • Reduces risk by limiting the scope of each change通过限制每次变更的范围来降低风险
  • Makes testing more focused and effective让测试更聚焦、更有效
  • Makes code reviews more manageable让代码评审更可控
  • Allows for easier troubleshooting if issues arise出问题时更容易排查

This may mean pushing back on feature requests if they are too large and breaking them into smaller features to control the size of the change. Remember that it’s better to deliver several small, successful changes than one large change that introduces bugs.

这可能意味着如果功能请求太大，你要顶回去，把它拆成更小的功能以控制变更规模。记住：交付几个小而成功的改动，胜过一个引入 bug 的大改动。

Let’s say that you receive a request to modify the way your system will process an order. In the following example, you can see that the process order already does too much and is a candidate for refactoring. Instead of trying to change the logic for the entire method, consider breaking some of the functionality into smaller methods, writing tests for those methods, and validating that each works correctly before moving on to another one:

假设你收到一个请求，要修改系统处理订单的方式。在下面的例子中，你可以看到 processOrder 已经做了太多事，是重构的候选对象。不要试图一次性改整个方法的逻辑，而是考虑把部分功能拆成更小的方法、为这些方法写测试，并在进入下一个之前验证每个都正确工作：

// Instead of changing this entire method at once...
public void processOrder(Order order) {
    // Validate order
    // Calculate totals
    // Apply discounts
    // Calculate shipping
    // Apply taxes
    // Process payment
    // Update inventory
    // Send confirmation
}

// Break it down into smaller, separate changes:
// 1. First, extract the validation logic
private boolean validateOrder(Order order) {
    // Validation logic here
    return isValid;
}

// 2. Next, extract the totals calculation
private double calculateOrderTotal(Order order) {
    // Total calculation logic here
    return total;
}

// 3. Continue with other extractions, testing after each change

Version control best practices

Most of the new projects you work on probably already have version control in place. In some scenarios, you might find yourself working with existing code that lacks proper version control or might need to establish best practices from the start:

你参与的大多数新项目可能已经有版本控制。在某些场景下，你可能会发现自己在处理缺乏恰当版本控制的既有代码，或者需要从零开始建立最佳实践：

  • Legacy codebases — you may encounter older projects that have version control but lack best practices. These applications might commit everything to main with no branching strategy in place. They might contain inconsistent commit messages, massive unmerged changes, and repositories with generated files or dependencies that should have never been tracked in the first place.遗留代码库——你可能遇到有版本控制但缺乏最佳实践的老项目。这些应用可能把所有东西都提交到 main、没有分支策略。它们可能包含不一致的提交信息、大量未合并的改动，以及跟踪了本不该跟踪的生成文件或依赖的仓库。
  • Personal or small-scale projects — when starting your own projects or working in very small teams, it’s tempting to skip version control. You might think “it’s just me” or “we can communicate directly,” but establishing good habits early prevents technical debt and makes it easier when the project grows or when you need to onboard others.个人或小型项目——开始自己的项目或在极小团队工作时，跳过版本控制很有诱惑力。你可能觉得“就我一个人”或“我们可以直接沟通”，但早点建立好习惯能防止技术债，让项目成长或需要带新人时更容易。
  • Open source contributions — when forking repositories or contributing to open source projects, you need to understand and follow the project’s version control conventions while maintaining your own fork properly.开源贡献——fork 仓库或为开源项目做贡献时，你需要理解并遵循项目的版本控制约定，同时妥善维护自己的 fork。
  • Contractor or consultant work — when joining existing projects, you may need to establish or improve version control practices that weren’t previously prioritized.外包或顾问工作——加入既有项目时，你可能需要建立或改善此前未被重视的版本控制实践。

No matter which scenario you find yourself in, version control systems like Git are essential for making safe changes to existing codebases. When used effectively, they provide safety nets that allow you to experiment, track history, and collaborate without fear of losing work or breaking functionality.

无论你身处哪种场景，像 Git 这样的版本控制系统对安全地修改既有代码库都必不可少。有效使用时，它们提供安全网，让你可以试验、追踪历史、协作，而不必担心丢失工作或破坏功能。

Commit strategically. When working with existing code, your commits should tell a story of how the code evolved:

有策略地提交。在既有代码上工作时，你的提交应当讲一个代码如何演化的故事：

  • Make atomic commits — each commit should represent a single logical change that can stand on its own. This makes it easier to understand, review, and, if necessary, revert changes.做原子提交——每个提交应代表一个独立成立的单一逻辑变更。这让理解、评审以及（必要时）回退变更更容易。
原书第 140 页
  • Write meaningful commit messages — a good commit message explains both what changed and why. Future developers (including your future self) will thank you for the context. The following code demonstrates good and bad commit message examples:写有意义的提交信息——好的提交信息既解释改了什么，也解释为什么。后来的开发者（包括未来的你）会因你提供的上下文感谢你。下面的代码展示了好的和坏的提交信息示例：
# Poor commit message
Fix bug

# Better commit message
Fix order calculation when a discount code is applied twice

The system was double-applying discount codes when customers
entered them in both mobile and desktop sessions. This fix
ensures the discount is only applied once per order.
  • Commit frequently — don’t wait until you’ve made dozens of changes before committing. Small, frequent logical commits make it easier to identify when and where issues were introduced.频繁提交——不要等到做了几十处改动才提交。小而频繁的逻辑提交让你更容易识别问题是何时、何地引入的。

Branch wisely. Branching strategies will vary by organization, team, and project, but certain principles will apply when working on existing code:

明智地分支。分支策略因组织、团队和项目而异，但在既有代码上工作时，有些原则通用：

  • Create feature branches — isolate your changes in a dedicated branch until they’re ready for integration. This keeps the main branch stable and allows you to experiment freely.创建特性分支——把你的改动隔离在专用分支上，直到准备好集成。这保持主分支稳定，让你自由试验。
  • Keep branches short-lived — long-lived branches diverge further from the main codebase over time, making integration more difficult. Aim to merge your changes back within days, not weeks.保持分支短命——长寿分支随时间与主代码库越来越分叉，让集成更困难。目标是几天内（而不是几周内）把改动合并回去。
  • Rebase before merging — when appropriate, rebase your changes on top of the latest main branch to ensure you’re working with the most current version of the codebase. Important: rebasing rewrites commit history, so use it carefully on shared branches.合并前变基——适当时，把你的变基在最新主分支之上，确保你用的是代码库最新版本。重要：变基会重写提交历史，所以在共享分支上要谨慎使用。

Pull requests and code reviews. A PR is a developer’s proposal to merge changes from one branch into another, opening the work for review, discussion, and automated checks before integration. You will want to keep your PRs focused and manageable. A PR that changes 1,000 lines of code across 20 files is difficult to review. Instead, aim for smaller, focused PRs that address a single concern.

拉取请求和代码评审。PR 是开发者把一个分支的改动合并到另一个分支的提案，在集成前让工作接受评审、讨论和自动检查。你要让 PR 聚焦、可控。一个跨 20 个文件改 1000 行的 PR 很难评审。相反，目标是更小、聚焦于单一关注点的 PR。

In the code review, make sure you explain what problem you’re solving and how your changes address it. Include any references you have to relevant issues or requirements. Code reviews are about improving the solution, not criticizing the developer. Be open to suggestions and willing to iterate on your approach.

在代码评审中，确保解释你在解决什么问题、你的改动如何解决它。附上你相关 issue 或需求的引用。代码评审是为了改进方案，不是为了批评开发者。对建议持开放态度，愿意迭代你的方法。

As you can see, although you shouldn’t charge into modifying existing codebases with wild abandon, there’s no need to be afraid of making a mark. Refactor safely with tests, follow the scout rule, and focus on small, reversible changes.

如你所见，虽然你不该横冲直撞地修改既有代码库，但也不必害怕留下自己的印记。带着测试安全重构、遵循童子军规则、专注于小而可逆的改动。

Wrapping Up

Working with existing code is one of those fundamental skills that can take you from coder to software engineer. Throughout this chapter, we’ve explored strategies for navigating, understanding, and safely modifying codebases. You’ve learned how to understand unfamiliar codebases by starting with the big picture, reviewing documentation, and grasping the project’s architecture. We’ve covered how to follow the execution flows by finding entry points, tracing request journeys, and identifying external dependencies. You now know how to build mental models incrementally by breaking down complex systems and visualizing relationships. We also examined how to make changes safely through careful refactoring, following the scout rule, and using version control best practices.

在既有代码上工作，是能让你从码农成长为软件工程师的基础技能之一。本章我们探索了导航、理解和安全修改代码库的策略。你学会了如何从全局入手、阅读文档、把握项目架构来理解陌生代码库。我们讲了如何通过找入口、跟踪请求旅程、识别外部依赖来跟随执行流。你现在知道如何通过拆解复杂系统和可视化关系来渐进建立心智模型。我们还考察了如何通过谨慎重构、遵循童子军规则、使用版本控制最佳实践来安全地做改动。

These skills aren’t just nice to have; they are essential for your growth as a software engineer. While creating new applications from scratch can be fun and exciting, the reality is that most of your career will involve working with existing code. Mastering these techniques will help you quickly and confidently contribute to any codebase, regardless of its size or complexity.

这些技能不是“有了更好”，而是你作为软件工程师成长所必需的。虽然从零创建新应用可能有趣又激动人心，但现实是你职业生涯的大部分时间都将在既有代码上工作。掌握这些技术会帮你快速、自信地为任何代码库做贡献，无论它规模多大、多复杂。

Putting It into Practice

Implementing what you’ve learned requires action, not just knowledge. The following practical steps will help you apply these code navigation and modification skills when working with existing code:

把学到的东西落地需要行动，而不只是知识。以下实操步骤帮你在既有代码上工作时应用这些代码导航和修改技能：

  1. Find an open source project that interests you and spend 30 minutes exploring its codebase without writing any code. Focus on understanding its structure and organization.找一个你感兴趣的开源项目，花 30 分钟浏览它的代码库，不写任何代码。专注理解它的结构和组织。
  2. Practice request tracing end-to-end by selecting a web application (like the PetClinic example) and tracing a complete user journey from UI interaction through API calls to database changes by using browser dev tools, logging, and debugging in sequence.选一个 Web 应用（如 PetClinic 例子）端到端地练习请求跟踪，依次使用浏览器开发者工具、日志和调试，跟踪从 UI 交互、经 API 调用到数据库变更的完整用户旅程。
  3. Pick a method from an open source project that’s difficult to understand and refactor it to improve readability without changing its behavior.从开源项目里挑一个难理解的方法，在不改变其行为的前提下重构它以提升可读性。
  4. Find a legacy project with minimal test coverage and practice adding tests that document existing behavior.找一个测试覆盖极少的遗留项目，练习补写记录既有行为的测试。
  5. Create a mental model diagram by picking one business process from a real codebase and create a visual representation (hand drawing, flowchart, sequence diagram, or component diagram) that shows how the code actually flows, then validate it with a team member.从真实代码库中挑一个业务流程，创建一张心智模型图（手绘、流程图、时序图或组件图），展示代码实际如何流转，然后和一位团队成员验证它。
  6. Make a complex change to an existing codebase by using small, reversible commits. Get feedback from a peer on your commit strategy.用小而可逆的提交对一个既有代码库做一次复杂改动。请同事就你的提交策略给反馈。
  7. Apply the scout rule to a project you’re working on by identifying three small improvements you can make to leave the code better than you found it.对你正在做的项目应用童子军规则，找出三处你可以做的小改进，让代码比你发现它时更好。
  8. Practice safe dependency changes by identifying an external dependency in a project and researching how to safely upgrade or replace it, including impact analysis and rollback planning.练习安全的依赖变更：在项目中识别一个外部依赖，研究如何安全升级或替换它，包括影响分析和回滚规划。
